Northstar Orchard Pilot Report
Fictional Internal Report - August 2026
Executive Summary
Northstar Orchard is a fictional precision-agriculture pilot operated by Arborline Labs in the town of
Bellweather. The pilot ran from 6 April 2026 through 28 July 2026 across three orchard blocks: Cedar,
Maple, and Juniper. Its goal was to test whether low-cost soil sensors, targeted irrigation, and weekly
drone surveys could reduce water use without lowering fruit quality.

Block Performance
Cedar block produced the largest water saving at 26.1%. Maple block saved 19.8%, while Juniper
saved 18.9%. Juniper had the highest fruit-size improvement at 4.7%, but it also experienced the most
sensor maintenance events because two moisture probes failed after heavy rain on 14 June.

The irrigation controller was configured with a soil-moisture trigger of 24%. If a block's median reading
fell below that threshold for two consecutive sampling windows, a 22-minute irrigation cycle was
scheduled. The exception was Cedar block, where a 19-minute cycle was used because its soil retained
water longer.

Operational Findings
The most useful operational change was not the sensor hardware itself, but the combination of sensor
readings with drone-derived canopy temperature. During the pilot, the team classified a block as
irrigation-priority when median soil moisture was below threshold and canopy temperature exceeded
the block's seven-day rolling average by at least 2.4 degrees Celsius.
A false alarm occurred on 3 July in Maple block when a drone image showed an apparent hot zone.

Field inspection found that the cause was reflective bird-netting rather than plant stress. After that event,
the team added a manual verification step before scheduling any emergency irrigation based only on

Cost Notes
The approved pilot budget was INR 18.75 lakh. Final recorded spend was INR 17.92 lakh. The largest
categories were drone operations at INR 5.10 lakh, sensors and gateways at INR 4.65 lakh,
irrigation-control upgrades at INR 3.20 lakh, and field staffing at INR 2.95 lakh. The remaining a

covered travel, replacement parts, and data storage.
Recommendation
The team recommended extending the system for one additional season before any large-scale
deployment. The next phase, internally named ORBIT-18, should include at least 60 hectares, introduce
automatic probe-health checks, and compare two irrigation thresholds instead of one.

compare two irrigation thresholds instead of one.
The review board specifically decided not to automate emergency irrigation in the next phase.
Emergency cycles must remain human-approved until the false-positive rate of image-based alerts falls
below 2%. The target date for the ORBIT-18 readiness review is 12 February 2027.
